title: An explicit finite-time stability criterion for fuzzy fractional delay differential equations with generalized Caputo derivatives
author: Khadija Elhakimy; Ismail Sadouki; Ali El Mfadel; Said Melliani
work: Finite-time stability for fuzzy fractional delay differential equations with generalized Caputo derivatives
source_version: Electronic Journal of Differential Equations 2026, No. 07, pp. 1--14; DOI 10.58997/ejde.2026.07; publisher version
difficulty_reason: The counted theorem needs a source-local stability mechanism rather than a routine corollary: the authors dominate the distance functional to the fuzzy zero by a psi-weighted generalized Caputo integral of the delayed right-hand side using assumption (A2), pass to the nondecreasing envelope of the distance to absorb the delay term, verify that the auxiliary functional built on the psi generalized kernel is nondecreasing, and then invoke a generalized Gronwall inequality with the Mittag-Leffler function to convert the explicit solution formula into the quantitative criterion delta times E_{beta,1}(2 L D^beta) not exceeding epsilon. This is a genuine two-sided fuzzy gH-arithmetic estimate for a delay system governed by a psi-generalized Caputo derivative, hence above ordinary PhD qualification exercises, but it stays at estimate-tracking level rather than introducing a new structural mechanism, so it is graded H2 rather than H3.
